text: In Scratch, what is the term for the characters or objects that appear on the stage?
explanation: Sprites are the characters or objects in a Scratch project. They can have costumes, sounds, and scripts attached to them.

text: Which Scratch block will repeat a set of instructions exactly 10 times?
explanation: The 'repeat 10' block is a loop that runs the blocks inside it exactly 10 times before continuing.

text: Which Microsoft Word feature lets you change the margin size on a page?
explanation: In Word, margins are adjusted through the Page Layout (or Layout) tab using the Margins option.

text: To add a new row at the bottom of a Word table, you can press which key while the cursor is in the last cell?
explanation: Pressing Tab in the last cell of a Word table automatically adds a new row at the bottom.

text: Which HTML tag is used to create the largest heading on a webpage?
explanation: <h1> defines the most important (largest) heading. Headings go from <h1> (largest) to <h6> (smallest).

text: Which CSS property changes the text colour of an element?
explanation: The 'color' property sets the foreground (text) colour of an element in CSS.

text: In Small Basic, which object is used to display text on the screen?
explanation: TextWindow is the Small Basic object for text-based output (and input). Use TextWindow.WriteLine() to print text.

text: Which view in PowerPoint shows all slides as small thumbnails in sequence?
explanation: Slide Sorter view displays all slides as thumbnails, making it easy to reorder or delete slides.

text: In Excel, which function adds up all values in the range A1 to A10?
explanation: =SUM(A1:A10) is the correct Excel formula to add all values from cell A1 through A10.

text: Which of the following best describes a computer?
options: An electronic device that processes data according to instructions
A machine that only stores information
A device that only outputs information
A tool used only for communication
explanation: A computer is an electronic device that accepts input, processes it according to stored instructions, and produces output.

text: In the IPO model, what does the letter 'P' stand for?
explanation: IPO stands for Input – Processing – Output, the three fundamental stages of how a computer handles data.

text: Which of the following is an example of information rather than raw data?
options: A list of unprocessed test scores
A set of survey responses before analysis
explanation: Information is data that has been processed and given meaning. A calculated average is processed data, making it information.

text: What is the primary purpose of the internet?
options: To connect computers and devices globally for communication and data sharing
To store all the world's data in one place
To control all computers from a central server
To run programs faster on local machines
explanation: The internet is a global network of interconnected computers and devices that enables communication and data sharing worldwide.

text: Which practice best protects your online accounts from being hacked?
options: Using strong, unique passwords for each account
Using the same simple password everywhere
Sharing your password with trusted friends
explanation: Strong, unique passwords for each account reduce the risk that a breach on one site compromises other accounts.

text: Which of the following is an OUTPUT device?
explanation: A monitor displays information from the computer, making it an output device. Keyboards, mice, and scanners are input devices.

text: In Logo programming, which command moves the turtle forward by 50 steps?
explanation: FORWARD (or FD) 50 moves the Logo turtle forward by 50 units in the direction it is currently facing.

text: What is a folder (directory) used for on a computer?
options: To organise and group related files together
explanation: Folders (directories) are used to organise files into groups, making it easier to find and manage them.

text: Which part of the Windows desktop shows the time, date, and system icons?
explanation: The taskbar (specifically the system tray or notification area) at the bottom of the screen shows the clock, date, and system icons.

text: Which keyboard shortcut makes selected text bold in most word processors?
explanation: Ctrl + B applies bold formatting to selected text in most word-processing applications.

text: In Microsoft Word, which feature lets you apply a pre-designed combination of fonts, colours, and effects to text?
explanation: Styles in Word are named sets of formatting (font, size, colour, spacing) that can be applied to text with one click.

text: What does URL stand for?
explanation: URL stands for Uniform Resource Locator — the web address used to locate a specific resource on the internet.

text: In PowerPoint, what is each individual page of a presentation called?
explanation: Each page in a PowerPoint presentation is called a slide. A presentation is made up of one or more slides.

text: Which PowerPoint feature controls how one slide transitions to the next during a slideshow?
explanation: Transitions are visual effects that appear between slides. Animations apply to objects within a slide.

text: What generation of computers first used transistors instead of vacuum tubes?
explanation: Second-generation computers (late 1950s–early 1960s) replaced vacuum tubes with transistors, making them smaller and more reliable.

text: Which storage medium uses laser light to read and write data?
explanation: Optical discs (CDs, DVDs, Blu-rays) use a laser beam to read and write data stored as tiny pits on the disc surface.

text: In Microsoft Word, which menu option do you use to insert a table into your document?
explanation: Tables are inserted via the Insert tab in Microsoft Word. You can choose the number of rows and columns.

text: In PowerPoint, what is the difference between an animation and a transition?
options: Animations apply to objects on a slide; transitions apply between slides
Transitions apply to objects on a slide; animations apply between slides
Animations only work on text, transitions only work on images
explanation: Animations control how objects (text, images) appear or move on a slide. Transitions control how the whole slide changes to the next.

text: Which key starts a PowerPoint slideshow from the beginning?
explanation: Pressing F5 starts the slideshow from the first slide. Shift+F5 starts from the current slide.

text: What is the purpose of a search engine?
options: To find and index web pages based on keywords
To store your personal files online
explanation: A search engine (e.g. Google) crawls and indexes the web so users can find pages relevant to their search keywords.

text: Which of the following is NOT a type of multimedia?
explanation: Multimedia refers to content that uses a combination of text, audio, images, video, and animation. A spreadsheet formula is not multimedia.

text: In Scratch, which block category contains the 'move 10 steps' block?
explanation: The Motion category contains blocks that control sprite movement, including 'move 10 steps' and 'turn' blocks.

text: In Scratch, what does the 'broadcast' block do?
options: Sends a message that other sprites can receive and respond to
Moves the sprite to a random position
explanation: Broadcast sends a named message to all sprites. Any sprite with a 'when I receive' block listening for that message will run its script.

text: What is a sensor in the context of robotics?
options: A device that detects information from the environment
A motor that moves the robot
The battery that powers the robot
explanation: Sensors detect environmental inputs (light, temperature, distance, etc.) and convert them into signals the robot can process.

text: What is the main purpose of mail merge in Microsoft Word?
options: To personalise a document (e.g. a letter) with data from a list
To merge two Word documents into one
To send emails directly from Word
explanation: Mail merge combines a template document with a data source (e.g. a spreadsheet) to produce personalised copies for each recipient.

text: Which email field should you use to send a copy of a message to someone who is not the main recipient?
explanation: CC (Carbon Copy) sends a visible copy to extra recipients. BCC sends a copy without other recipients seeing the address.

text: In Excel, what is a cell reference?
options: The address of a cell, e.g. B3
The formula entered in a cell
The value displayed in a cell
explanation: A cell reference (e.g. B3) identifies a specific cell by its column letter and row number. It is used in formulas to refer to that cell's value.

text: Which Excel shortcut key opens the Find & Replace dialog?
explanation: Ctrl + H opens Find & Replace in Excel, letting you find specific text and replace it. Ctrl + F opens Find only.

text: In Excel, what does 'wrap text' formatting do to a cell?
options: Displays long text on multiple lines within the cell
Shrinks the text to fit the cell width
Merges the cell with the one next to it
explanation: Wrap Text makes long cell content display on multiple lines within the same cell rather than overflowing into adjacent cells.

text: Which flowchart symbol is used to represent a decision (yes/no question)?
explanation: A diamond shape in a flowchart represents a decision point, typically a yes/no or true/false condition.

text: In Scratch, which block lets you sense whether the mouse button is being pressed?
explanation: 'mouse down?' is a sensing block that reports true when the mouse button is currently held down.

text: In QB64 (QuickBASIC), which keyword is used to display text on the screen?
explanation: The PRINT keyword in QB64/QBasic outputs text or values to the console screen.

text: What is the decimal value of the binary number 1011?
In Excel, which formula correctly calculates the average of cells B2 to B8?
explanation: =AVERAGE(B2:B8) is the correct Excel function to calculate the arithmetic mean of cells B2 through B8.

text: Which Excel feature arranges data from lowest to highest value?
explanation: Sort Ascending arranges data from smallest to largest (numbers) or A to Z (text).

text: Which chart type is most suitable for showing how a value changes over time?
explanation: Line charts are best for showing trends and changes over a continuous period of time.

text: Which protocol is used to securely transfer web pages over the internet?
explanation: HTTPS (Hypertext Transfer Protocol Secure) encrypts data between the browser and web server, making it the secure version of HTTP.

text: Which HTML tag creates a hyperlink?
explanation: The <a> (anchor) tag creates hyperlinks. The href attribute specifies the destination URL.

text: What does the HTML tag's 'alt' attribute do?
options: Provides alternative text if the image cannot be displayed
Aligns the image on the page
Adds a caption below the image
explanation: The alt attribute supplies descriptive alternative text shown when an image fails to load, and is also read by screen readers.

text: Which of the following is an example of machine learning?
options: A spam filter that improves by analysing thousands of emails
A remote control turning on a TV
A thermostat set to a fixed temperature
explanation: Machine learning systems improve their performance by learning patterns from large amounts of data, unlike rule-based programs.

text: In QB64, which statement is used to receive input from the user during program execution?
explanation: The INPUT statement pauses program execution, displays an optional prompt, and stores what the user types into a variable.

text: Which Python function is used to display output on the screen?
explanation: print() is the built-in Python function for outputting text and values to the console.

text: What type of AI task involves teaching a computer to recognise cats in photos?
explanation: Image classification is an AI task where a model is trained to assign labels (e.g. 'cat') to images.

text: What is the Internet of Things (IoT)?
options: A network of everyday physical devices connected to the internet
explanation: IoT refers to everyday objects (smart watches, fridges, sensors) embedded with technology that allows them to connect and exchange data over the internet.

text: In Microsoft Access, what is a table?
options: A structured collection of data organised in rows (records) and columns (fields)
A visual form for entering data
A printed summary of database information
explanation: In a database, a table stores data in rows (records) and columns (fields). It is the fundamental storage unit in Access.

text: In Access, what is the purpose of a primary key?
options: To uniquely identify each record in a table
To lock the database from editing
explanation: A primary key is a field (or set of fields) whose value is unique for every record, allowing each row to be identified unambiguously.

text: What is the purpose of a report in Microsoft Access?
options: To present database data in a formatted, printable layout
To enter new records into a table
explanation: Reports format and present database information for printing or viewing, often summarising or grouping data from queries or tables.

text: What does 'bandwidth' refer to in networking?
options: The maximum amount of data that can be transmitted per second
The number of devices on a network
The security level of a network
explanation: Bandwidth is the capacity of a network connection, measured in bits per second (bps). Higher bandwidth means more data can be sent per second.

text: Which Google app is best suited for creating and collaborating on a spreadsheet online?
explanation: Google Sheets is the Google Workspace equivalent of Microsoft Excel — an online spreadsheet application with real-time collaboration.

text: What type of malware disguises itself as legitimate software to trick users into installing it?
explanation: A Trojan horse appears to be a useful program but secretly carries malicious code. Unlike viruses, Trojans do not replicate themselves.

text: Which HTML tag defines a data cell within a table row?
explanation: <td> (table data) defines a standard data cell. <th> defines a header cell. <tr> defines a row. <table> defines the table itself.

text: What is cyberbullying?
options: Using digital technology to harass, threaten, or embarrass another person
Installing harmful software on someone's computer
explanation: Cyberbullying is the use of electronic communication (social media, messaging) to bully, intimidate, or harm another person.

text: A computer is running very slowly. Which of the following is the FIRST troubleshooting step?
explanation: Restarting clears temporary files and memory and often resolves performance issues. It is always the first and simplest troubleshooting step.

text: In Python, which keyword starts a function definition?
explanation: In Python, functions are defined using the 'def' keyword, followed by the function name and parentheses, e.g. def greet():

text: What is the role of the Control Unit (CU) within the CPU?
options: It directs the operation of the processor by interpreting and executing instructions
It performs arithmetic and logical operations
It stores frequently used data temporarily
It manages input and output operations
explanation: The Control Unit fetches, decodes, and executes instructions. It coordinates the activities of the CPU and other hardware components.

text: Which type of memory loses its contents when the computer is switched off?
explanation: RAM (Random Access Memory) is volatile — its contents are lost when power is removed. ROM and flash memory are non-volatile.

text: Which of the following is a direct-entry input device?
explanation: A barcode scanner reads data directly without the user typing it, making it a direct-entry (automatic) input device.

text: During which stage of the Fetch-Decode-Execute cycle is the instruction retrieved from main memory?
explanation: In the Fetch stage, the CPU retrieves the next instruction from main memory using the address stored in the Program Counter (PC).

text: Which of the following is an example of an embedded system?
options: The control system inside a microwave oven
A laptop connected to the internet
explanation: An embedded system is a dedicated computer system built into a device to control a specific function, like the controller inside a microwave.

text: Which secondary storage device has no moving parts and uses flash memory?
explanation: SSDs store data in flash memory chips with no moving mechanical parts, making them faster and more shock-resistant than HDDs.

text: Which of the following is NOT a function of an operating system?
explanation: Editing a document is done by application software. The OS manages hardware resources, memory, I/O, and provides a UI for applications to run on.

text: What does a compiler do?
options: Translates the entire high-level source code into machine code before execution
Translates and executes source code one line at a time
Converts machine code back into source code
Checks source code for logic errors only
explanation: A compiler translates the whole high-level program into machine code in one go, producing an executable file. An interpreter translates line by line at run time.

text: What is the purpose of DNS (Domain Name System)?
options: To translate domain names (e.g. www.google.com) into IP addresses
To encrypt web traffic between client and server
To assign IP addresses to devices on a network
To filter inappropriate content on the internet
explanation: DNS acts like a phonebook for the internet, converting human-readable domain names into numerical IP addresses that computers use to route traffic.

text: What is the output of an AND gate when both inputs are 1?
explanation: An AND gate outputs 1 only when ALL inputs are 1. With both inputs at 1, the output is 1.

text: How many different values can be represented with 4 bits?
explanation: With n bits you can represent 2ⁿ values. With 4 bits: 2⁴ = 16 possible values (0 through 15).

text: Convert the hexadecimal number 2F to binary.
explanation: 2 in hex = 0010 in binary; F in hex = 1111 in binary. Combined: 00101111.

text: Using 8-bit two's complement, what is the decimal value of 11111110?
explanation: For two's complement: 11111110 → invert bits = 00000001, add 1 = 00000010 = 2. Because MSB is 1 the number is negative: -2.

text: What is the main advantage of Unicode over ASCII for text representation?
options: Unicode supports a much larger range of characters including non-Latin scripts
Unicode uses fewer bits per character
Unicode is only used for programming languages
explanation: ASCII uses 7 bits and covers only 128 characters (English). Unicode (e.g. UTF-8/UTF-16) supports over a million characters including Arabic, Chinese, emoji, etc.

text: Which factor has the greatest effect on the file size of a digital audio recording?
explanation: File size = sample rate × bit depth × duration × channels. Higher sample rate and bit depth produce better quality but larger files.

text: What is a pixel?
options: The smallest unit of a digital image, representing a single point of colour
A unit of image file size
The resolution of a display screen
A type of image file format
explanation: A pixel (picture element) is the smallest unit of a digital image. Each pixel has a colour value; together they form the complete image.

text: What is the key difference between lossy and lossless compression?
options: Lossy removes some data permanently; lossless allows perfect reconstruction of the original
Lossless removes data permanently; lossy keeps the original intact
Lossy is always smaller than lossless
They are the same process with different names
explanation: Lossy compression (e.g. JPEG, MP3) discards some data for smaller files. Lossless compression (e.g. PNG, FLAC) reduces size without losing any data.

text: What is the base (radix) of the hexadecimal number system?
explanation: Hexadecimal is base-16, using digits 0–9 and letters A–F to represent values 0–15.

text: Which file format is typically used for lossless image compression?
explanation: PNG uses lossless compression — no image data is discarded, making it suitable for graphics that require sharp edges.

text: Run-length encoding (RLE) is most effective for which type of data?
options: Data with many consecutive repeated values
explanation: RLE replaces runs of repeated values with a count and a single value. It is highly effective when data has long sequences of the same value (e.g. simple images).

text: What is the purpose of the TCP/IP protocol suite?
options: To define rules for how data is sent and received over the internet
To assign domain names to websites
To detect viruses on a network
explanation: TCP/IP is the foundational set of communication protocols for the internet, governing how data is packetised, addressed, transmitted, routed, and received.

text: What is a MAC address?
options: A unique hardware identifier assigned to a network interface card
A software address assigned by a DHCP server
A URL for accessing a website
A password for a wireless network
explanation: A MAC (Media Access Control) address is a 48-bit hardware identifier permanently assigned to a network interface by its manufacturer.

text: What is a variable in programming?
options: A named storage location in memory that holds a value
A fixed value that never changes
A function that returns a result
explanation: A variable is a named container in memory whose value can be read, changed, or used during program execution.

text: What is the time complexity of a linear search on a list of n items in the worst case?
explanation: In the worst case, linear search checks every element once, giving O(n) time complexity.

text: What is phishing?
options: A fraudulent attempt to obtain sensitive information by pretending to be a trustworthy source
Installing a program that monitors keystrokes
Flooding a server with traffic to make it unavailable
Encrypting a victim's files and demanding a ransom
explanation: Phishing tricks users (typically via fake emails or websites) into revealing passwords, credit card numbers, or other sensitive data.

text: Which of the following is a cultural influence on product design?
options: Designing a product that reflects the traditions and values of a specific community
Choosing cheaper materials to reduce cost
Making a product as small as possible
Using only one colour throughout the design
explanation: Cultural influences include local traditions, aesthetics, symbols, and values that shape what a product looks like or how it is used.

text: What is the purpose of a design brief?
options: To clearly define the design problem and outline what the final product must achieve
To list the tools needed for manufacturing
To provide a detailed manufacturing plan
To record the cost of materials used
explanation: A design brief is a short written statement that identifies the design problem and sets the goals, constraints, and requirements the solution must meet.

text: Why is it important to produce multiple design proposals before choosing one?
options: It allows comparison of different ideas and selection of the most suitable solution
It is a legal requirement for product design
It makes the final product cheaper
It reduces the need for a design brief
explanation: Multiple proposals widen the solution space, allow evaluation against design criteria, and reduce the risk of overlooking a better solution.

text: What does a production plan (manufacturing plan) include?
options: The sequence of steps, tools, materials, and time needed to make the product
The final selling price of the product
A drawing of what the product will look like
User feedback on the finished product
explanation: A production plan sets out the order of manufacturing operations, the tools and materials required, and estimated time for each step.

text: Against what should a final product be evaluated?
explanation: A design specification lists the measurable criteria the product must meet. Evaluating against it gives an objective measure of success.

text: What is a design specification?
options: A detailed list of criteria the design solution must meet
A rough sketch of a possible solution
explanation: A design specification is a precise list of requirements (size, function, safety, cost, aesthetics) that the final solution must satisfy.

text: What is the purpose of a prototype in the design process?
options: To test and evaluate a design idea before full production
explanation: A prototype is a working model used to test how well a design meets its specification, identify problems, and inform improvements.

text: Which method is used to evaluate a design against specific, measurable criteria?
options: Comparing the product point by point against the design specification
Asking a friend if they like it
Counting the number of design proposals made
Measuring only the cost of production
explanation: Systematic evaluation checks each criterion in the specification (e.g. dimensions, function, safety) against the actual product.

text: Which drawing technique shows a 3D object with three faces visible, drawn along axes at 30° to the horizontal?
explanation: Isometric drawing uses axes at 30° to show three faces of an object simultaneously, giving a 3D appearance without vanishing points.

text: Which of the following is a reason to wear safety goggles when working in a workshop?
options: To protect the eyes from flying particles, dust, or chemical splashes
To improve vision in low light
To identify the correct tool to use
explanation: Safety goggles are personal protective equipment (PPE) that shield eyes from hazards such as debris, sparks, or chemical splashes.

text: Which of the following is a thermoplastic?
explanation: Thermoplastics (e.g. acrylic, PET, HDPE) soften when heated and can be reshaped. Thermosets (e.g. fibreglass, melamine) permanently harden when cured.

text: What is vacuum forming used to produce?
options: Thin plastic sheets moulded into 3D shapes
explanation: Vacuum forming heats a thermoplastic sheet, drapes it over a mould, then uses vacuum pressure to pull it into the mould shape.

text: Before using a power tool, what should always be checked first?
options: That the tool is in good working order and guards are in place
That the tool matches the colour of the workpiece
That no one else is watching
That the tool is the most expensive available
explanation: Pre-use checks ensure guards are fitted, cables are undamaged, and the tool functions correctly — preventing accidents during use.

text: What is a triangulated structure?
options: A structure strengthened by arranging members in triangles to distribute loads
A structure built from three identical parts
A structure that can only support vertical loads
A structure made entirely from triangular cross-section beams
explanation: Triangulation rigidifies a structure by converting bending forces into tension and compression through triangular arrangements of members (e.g. in trusses).

text: What is a gear ratio?
options: The ratio of the number of teeth on the driver gear to the number of teeth on the driven gear
The speed of the motor in rpm
The size of the gear wheel
The force applied to the gear
explanation: Gear ratio = teeth on driver ÷ teeth on driven gear. It determines the change in speed and torque between the two gears.

text: Which validation check ensures that a number entered falls within an acceptable range?
explanation: A range check tests whether a value is between a specified minimum and maximum (e.g. a month number must be 1–12).

text: What is a firewall?
options: A system that monitors and controls incoming and outgoing network traffic based on security rules
A hardware device used to boost Wi-Fi signal
explanation: A firewall filters network traffic using predefined security rules to allow or block data packets, protecting a network from unauthorised access.

text: In asymmetric encryption, what is used to encrypt a message that only the recipient can decrypt?
explanation: In asymmetric (public-key) encryption, the sender encrypts with the recipient's public key. Only the recipient's private key can decrypt it.

text: Which type of sensor would be used to detect how bright it is in a room?
explanation: An LDR (light dependent resistor) changes its electrical resistance in response to light intensity, making it suitable for measuring brightness.

text: What is the purpose of an actuator in an automated system?
options: To convert a control signal into physical movement or action
To detect changes in the environment
To process and interpret sensor data
To store instructions for the system
explanation: Actuators (motors, servos, solenoids) receive electrical signals from the controller and produce mechanical movement or other physical effects.

text: What does a neural network use to improve its accuracy over time?
options: Training data and adjustment of weights between nodes
explanation: A neural network is trained by feeding it labelled examples and adjusting connection weights using algorithms (e.g. backpropagation) to minimise errors.

text: What is a qubit in quantum computing?
options: The quantum equivalent of a classical bit, which can exist in a superposition of 0 and 1
A unit of classical computing memory
A type of quantum processor chip
explanation: A qubit can be in a superposition of both 0 and 1 simultaneously (until measured), enabling quantum computers to process many states in parallel.

text: What is abstraction in problem-solving and programming?
options: Removing unnecessary details to focus on the essential aspects of a problem
Writing code as quickly as possible
Breaking a problem into smaller sub-problems
explanation: Abstraction simplifies complexity by hiding irrelevant details and representing only what is necessary to solve the problem.

text: Which sorting algorithm repeatedly finds the smallest unsorted element and places it in the correct position?
explanation: Selection sort scans the unsorted portion to find the minimum element and swaps it into its correct position, repeating until sorted.

text: Simplify the Boolean expression: A AND NOT A
explanation: A AND NOT A is a contradiction — a variable and its complement can never both be true at the same time, so the result is always 0.

text: What is the purpose of a test plan when developing software?
options: To document what inputs will be tested, expected outputs, and whether tests passed
To describe the user interface design
To list the programming languages used
explanation: A test plan specifies test cases (normal, boundary, erroneous data), expected results, and records actual outcomes to verify software correctness.

text: In the system development life cycle, what happens during the analysis stage?
options: The current system is investigated and requirements for the new system are identified
The new system is coded and built
The completed system is handed over to users
The system is tested with real data
explanation: Analysis involves studying the existing system, identifying problems, and defining what the new or improved system must do (requirements gathering).

text: Which SQL keyword is used to retrieve data from a database table?
explanation: SELECT is the SQL command for querying a database. It specifies which columns to return and can be combined with WHERE, ORDER BY, etc.

text: What is the worst-case time complexity of binary search?
explanation: Binary search halves the search space with each comparison, giving O(log n) worst-case time complexity.

text: In Python, what does the 'open()' function return when used to read a file?
options: A file object that can be iterated or read with methods like .read() or .readlines()
The entire file contents as a string immediately
A list of filenames in the directory
explanation: open() returns a file object. You then call methods such as .read(), .readline(), or .readlines() on it to access the file's content.

text: How many bytes are needed to store a single character in UTF-16 encoding (minimum)?
explanation: UTF-16 uses a minimum of 2 bytes (16 bits) per character for the Basic Multilingual Plane, compared to ASCII's 1 byte.

text: What is the difference between a LAN and a WAN?
options: A LAN covers a small geographic area; a WAN covers a large geographic area
A LAN uses wireless only; a WAN uses wired only
A WAN is faster than a LAN
A LAN requires an internet connection; a WAN does not
explanation: LAN (Local Area Network) covers a limited area such as a building. WAN (Wide Area Network) spans large geographic areas, often connecting multiple LANs.

text: What is De Morgan's first law?
options: NOT(A AND B) = NOT A OR NOT B
NOT(A OR B) = NOT A AND NOT B
A AND B = B AND A
explanation: De Morgan's first law: NOT(A AND B) ≡ NOT A OR NOT B. This allows conversion between AND and OR gates using inverters.

text: What is pipelining in a CPU?
options: Overlapping the fetch, decode, and execute stages of multiple instructions simultaneously
Reducing the clock speed to save energy
explanation: Pipelining allows different stages of multiple instructions to run concurrently, improving throughput. While one instruction is executing, the next is being decoded, and the one after is being fetched.

text: What is virtual memory?
options: A technique that uses secondary storage to extend the apparent size of RAM
Memory built directly into the CPU
explanation: Virtual memory uses a section of the hard drive as extra RAM, allowing the OS to run programs larger than physical RAM by swapping data in and out.

text: What does two-factor authentication (2FA) require?
options: Two separate forms of verification (e.g. password + one-time code)
Two different passwords for the same account
explanation: 2FA requires something you know (password) AND something you have (phone OTP) or something you are (biometrics), making unauthorised access much harder.

text: In machine learning, what is overfitting?
options: When a model learns the training data too well and performs poorly on new data
When a model is too simple to capture patterns in the data
When a model takes too long to train
When a model uses too much memory
explanation: Overfitting occurs when a model memorises training examples (including noise) instead of learning general patterns, causing poor generalisation to unseen data.

text: In Python, what mode string opens a file for appending new content without deleting existing content?
explanation: Opening a file with mode 'a' (append) positions the write pointer at the end of existing content, so new data is added without overwriting anything.

text: What is inheritance in object-oriented programming?
options: A mechanism where a child class derives attributes and methods from a parent class
Combining data and methods into a single unit
Hiding internal implementation details from the user
Creating multiple objects from the same class
explanation: Inheritance lets a subclass reuse (inherit) properties and behaviours from a superclass, enabling code reuse and a hierarchy of related classes.

text: Which data structure operates on a Last In, First Out (LIFO) principle?
explanation: A stack is LIFO — the last element added (pushed) is the first one removed (popped). A queue is FIFO.

text: What does Big O notation describe?
options: The growth rate of an algorithm's time or space requirements as input size increases
The exact running time of an algorithm in seconds
The number of lines of code in an algorithm
The programming language used to implement an algorithm
explanation: Big O notation expresses how the resource requirements (time or memory) of an algorithm scale with input size, independent of hardware or implementation details.

text: Which SQL clause filters the results of a SELECT query to rows that match a condition?
explanation: WHERE filters individual rows before any grouping. HAVING filters grouped results after GROUP BY.

text: What is the role of a device driver?
options: To allow the operating system to communicate with a specific hardware device
explanation: A device driver is software that acts as a translator between the OS and a hardware component (printer, graphics card, etc.), handling low-level communication.

text: What is a Karnaugh map (K-map) used for?
options: Simplifying Boolean expressions by grouping adjacent 1s in a grid
Calculating the clock speed of a CPU
explanation: A K-map is a visual tool for minimising Boolean expressions. Grouping adjacent 1s in powers of 2 allows common factors to be cancelled, simplifying the expression.
